assessments.reasoning: I independently retrieved and verified the exact bytes of Introduction to the 'RS' Portable Algol 68 Compiler and inspected the cited passage (§1, printed p. 2 (physical PDF p. 5)). TN802 §1 on printed page 2 identifies the compiler output as high-level stream language and assigns code production, representations and storage allocation to a second-pass translator.

challenge.method: Compare the two passes and the machine-dependent shell in the later RS compiler manual’s introductory diagram. Test whether stream language is either the source text or machine code.
challenge.results: The diagram confirms the intermediate stream boundary and a separate translation pass. It also identifies machine-dependent interfacing outside the portable compiler core.

limitations: This is the published RS architecture. It does not identify a particular completed port.
